notes: SHIP v1.14.401 - M2-a: THE GRAPHICS LIFECYCLE HAS AN OWNER. This opens M2, the iPhone WebGL unblock, and it is the structural half - RackEngine.attach, the reclaim barrier, modes and the vocabulary normalisation are M2-b and are NOT in this ship. THE ASYMMETRY BEING CLOSED. Two ad-hoc module globals tracked live GL contexts - _reh3dActive for the rack and _forge3dActive for the aisle - and the cross-dispose between them ran one way only. rackElevation_render3D disposed both. forge3d_render disposed only its own, because the guard against a live rack context sat one level up in forge3d_open. Any path that reached forge3d_render without going through that door left BOTH contexts live on a device with a ceiling of one. The guard was not enforced at the boundary that creates the renderer, so it was a convention someone had to remember, not an invariant. RackEngine is that boundary. Every renderer registers with it, and registration itself releases every other live attachment regardless of which module owns it - symmetric by construction, in one place, for every present and future caller. Spec invariant I1 is now structural. COVERAGE IS COMPLETE, AND THAT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The app contains exactly two new THREE.WebGLRenderer sites - the aisle and the rack - and both register. No renderer exists outside the engine. VISIBILITY, WHICH IS THE DRAIN NOBODY COULD SEE (spec I4). showMode disposed the Command hero, and only when leaving Command. Each renderer's own onVis checked document.hidden, which covers the app being backgrounded but is NOT set by a display:none ancestor. So leaving Build for Tools left the rack's animation loop running at full rate on a canvas nobody could see, for the rest of the shift, on a phone. Registration now installs an IntersectionObserver per attachment which drives named pause and resume operations on both renderers. It closes for every host without any caller having to remember, and the two loops keep their document.hidden path as well. R-05 HOLDS: this is ONE ENGINE, NOT ONE LOCATION. No presentation was removed, no scene internals were touched, RACK SCENE LOCK is intact - materials, the JOHN-LOCKED light rig, fog, tone mapping, tray geometry, type colours, bezel strips, floor, reflection and boot are all byte-identical. The diff is confined to the rack subsystem in one file, 121 insertions and 8 deletions. INSTRUMENTATION. PhantomGL.diag() gains an attachments line reading RackEngine.report(), which names each host, its kind, whether it is paused and whether it is still in the document. The legacy _reh3dActive and _forge3dActive assignments are retained as read-only shims so the M0 baseline instrument keeps reading true across the milestone; per the blueprint's instrumentation rule they and the standalone PhantomGL retire together at M2-b, and that condition is written into the code. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean, CSS braces 4557/4557 with a delta of 0, line endings unchanged at all-LF, scope checked - _rafId and frame are in forge3d_render's own scope and RackEngine is assigned top-level before any call site can run, three-stamp lockstep. DEVICE-VERIFY, and this is the point of the ship: (1) open Build, rack renders, then in Safari console run PhantomGL.diag() and confirm attachments shows exactly one entry for the Build mount. (2) Go Build to Open Aisle to Build. attachments must show ONE entry at every step - transferred, not added - and the rack must still be there on return. (3) Leave Build for Tools and confirm the Build attachment reports paused true; return to Build and confirm it reports paused false and the rack is animating again. (4) Enter Build ten times in a row and confirm attachments never exceeds one and the canvas count does not climb. (5) Everything else in the app should look and behave exactly as it did on .400.
